:::{#thm-rct-identification}
#### Identification of the ATE under randomization

If [consistency](#def-consistency) and
[unconditional exchangeability](#def-unconditional-exchangeability) hold,
and $0 < \Pf{A = 1} < 1$,
then for each treatment level $a \in \cb{0, 1}$,

$$\E{Y(a)} = \E{Y \mid A = a}$$

and therefore

$$\text{ATE} = \E{Y \mid A = 1} - \E{Y \mid A = 0}$$ {#eq-rct-ate}

:::

::: proof
For treatment level $a$:

$$
\ba
\E{Y(a)}
&= \E{Y(a) \mid A = a}
&& \text{(unconditional exchangeability: } Y(a) \ind A \text{)} \\
&= \E{Y \mid A = a}
&& \text{(consistency: } Y = Y(a) \text{ when } A = a \text{)}
\ea
$$

where the condition $0 < \Pf{A = 1} < 1$
makes both conditioning events $\cb{A = 1}$ and $\cb{A = 0}$ have positive probability.
Substituting into the [ATE](#def-ate):

$$
\ba
\text{ATE}
&= \E{Y(1)} - \E{Y(0)}
&& \text{(definition of ATE)} \\
&= \E{Y \mid A = 1} - \E{Y \mid A = 0}
&& \text{(apply the first result with } a = 1 \text{ and } a = 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::
